AFTER THE FACT -- N3 tested the filter N2 had already ruled out
(i) THE THREE-CANDIDATE PROBLEM. N2 tried three selectors and reported the one that
cleared p < 0.05 at p = 0.0475. Bonferroni over three
candidates puts that at 0.143, which does not clear. The breadth
selector is a lead, not an established result, and N2's PASS is generous.
(ii) THE FILTER N2 ACTUALLY POINTS AT: narrow ECs, not self-consistent ones.

this filter validates
(iii) WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PROPOSAL, plainly.
The 4x floor is CORRECT and now empirical -- it sits at the 60% percentile of
the measurements' own leave-one-out reproducibility (median 2.85x). That part of the
proposal is confirmed and is worth keeping.
What cannot be done yet is APPLYING it to the unmeasured majority. No selector
computable without the answer survives a proper test at n = 70, which is every gene
that has both a UniProt kcat and an EC with replicates. The bottleneck is not the
idea, it is that 70 validation points cannot establish a filter.
And the cost is steep even if it worked: 704 of 8,184 reactions (8.6%)
survive the self-consistency version, 5.4% of the model.
(iv) WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, given what is measured:
- the 704 self-consistent tier-1 reactions are the defensible core and can be
used as-is; they are not validated as BETTER, but they are measurements rather
than predictions, which is a different and sufficient reason
- the 5,941 CatPred reactions should carry the constant, because loop 124 measured
the constant at 9.42x against their 12.95x -- that swap needs no selector at all
- raising n is the only route to a validated filter, and the fetch that does it is
BRENDA's bulk file, currently behind a click-through licence with no static URL
